correctness.rationale: For any odd N≥3, positive couplings, deviations δ_i from antialignment obey sum δ_i=π mod2π. The exact energy difference from one frustrated weakest bond j is Σ_{i≠j} J_i(1−cos δ_i)−m(1−cos Σδ_i). Complex chord triangle inequality and weighted Cauchy give 1−cos Σδ_i≤(Σ1/J_i)Σ J_i(1−cosδ_i), implying global stability when ρ=mΣ1/J_i≤1. Equality ρ=1 rigid since at least two nonzero chord steps cannot saturate triangle inequality on a strictly convex circle. If ρ>1, perturb δ_i=ε/J_i shows negative quadratic difference, hence noncollinear global minimizers; perturbation also proves sharp coefficient. Independently checked rational 5-bond examples and 800 random configurations N=3,5,7,9. Global proof is analytic, not numerical.
residual_risks: Classical XY ring criterion is mathematically elementary once the weighted chord inequality is supplied; an older exact circuit/rigidity classification could dominate it.
